_meta.title: US police departments: racial disparity, racist conduct and links to white supremacist or far-right groups
_meta.what: Police and sheriff departments with documented findings: the two departments named on the Destruction page (with Police Scorecard figures), cases from the Brennan Center report on racism and white supremacy in law enforcement (each with the original court or news sources it cites), the eight Plain View Project roster jurisdictions, and US Justice Department pattern-or-practice findings of racial discrimination (with 2025 retractions noted).
_meta.licence: Facts with short quotations and links (fair use). Brennan Center pages: "© 2026 Brennan Center for Justice" (no open licence found). DOJ: US government work (public domain). Police Scorecard: terms page returned an error here (https://policescorecard.org/terms); figures are restated facts with a link. Coordinates: Wikidata, CC0.
_meta.notes: precision "city" = city-centre coordinate from Wikidata, not the department building; "address" = the agency item's own coordinate in Wikidata; "state" = no place named in the source (lat/lon null). Each record lists findings[] with year, plain summary, source and URL; quote fields are exact words from the source.

records.name: Columbus Division of Police
records.category: named on Destruction page; racial disparity
records.coord_source: Wikidata Q16567 (city coordinate, not the department HQ)

findings.summary: 66 killings by police; based on population a Black person was 5.2x as likely as a White person to be killed by police (Latinx 0.7x). Black people 2.5x more likely to be arrested for low-level offences. Overall score 37%.
findings.source: Police Scorecard (Campaign Zero)

findings.summary: Ohio Civil Rights Commission found "unlawful discriminatory practices": the division was slow to act on Black officers' complaints about a white sergeant who used racial slurs and talked of killing them.
findings.source: WOSU Public Media, 18 Jul 2016

findings.summary: Mayor Andrew Ginther asked the US Justice Department in April 2021 to review the division for racial bias; DOJ completed a review (not covering use of force).
findings.source: 10TV

records.note: The FiveThirtyEight article could not be read from here (redirects to ABC News; archive blocked), so its own figures are not included.

records.name: Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department
records.category: named on Destruction page; racial disparity; racist conduct
records.coord_source: Wikidata Q16565 (city coordinate, not the department HQ)

findings.summary: 37 killings by police; based on population a Black person was 2.7x as likely as a White person to be killed by police (Latinx 2x). Black people 8.3x more likely to be arrested for low-level offences. Overall score 59%.
findings.source: Police Scorecard (Campaign Zero)

findings.summary: Six officers involved in a racist text thread; three resigned and a review board recommended firing the other three. Sources described a contest over stopping the most Black drivers. The chief asked the US Justice Department to help investigate; the US Attorney is considering a civil rights investigation.
findings.source: WBTV (Connor Lomis), 15 Oct 2026

records.note: The FiveThirtyEight article could not be read from here, so its own figures are not included.

records.name: Anniston Police Department
records.coord_source: Wikidata Q79474 (city coordinate, not the department HQ)

findings.summary: City officials knew from 2009 that an officer belonged to the League of the South, a white supremacist secessionist group; he was promoted to lieutenant and fired only in 2015 after an SPLC article; a second lieutenant who attended the same rally was allowed to retire. A federal court upheld the firing.
findings.source: Mike German, "Hidden in Plain Sight: Racism, White Supremacy, and Far-Right Militancy in Law Enforcement", Brennan Center for Justice, 27 Aug 2020
original_sources_cited: Doggrell v. City of Anniston, 277 F. Supp. 3d 1239 (N.D. Ala. 2017), https://casetext.com/case/doggrell-v-city-of-anniston-1
